text:
ella: Hi all  first day! On a Surface Pro X (Windows ARM) docked at my desk. WireGuard says connected but CLI tools in WSL2 can't reach internal hosts (git.redwood.internal, registry.redwood.internal). Windows browser can reach them fine. Anyone seen docked Surface/USB-C NIC + VPN oddness?
it-support: Welcome Ella! That's a classic multi-NIC asymmetry. When you're docked you often have both the dock Ethernet + the built-in Wi-Fi/USB NICs. Windows chooses routes based on interface metrics; WSL2 uses the Windows routing table but sometimes a lower-metric (preferred) interface sends traffic out the wrong NIC while the VPN is bound to another adapter.
ella: How do I check which interface is preferred?
mark: Run in an admin PowerShell: `Get-NetIPInterface | Sort-Object InterfaceMetric` and `Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 10.240.0.0/16` to inspect where the VPC CIDR is routed. Also `ipconfig /all` helps identify the WireGuard adapter name.
ella: Ran those. The WireGuard adapter shows metric 50, dock Ethernet metric 10, and the route for 10.240.0.0/16 is via wg0 but the source IP is the dock's Ethernet and packets are leaving that interface.
alex: If packets leave the dock interface but the WireGuard server expects the VPN endpoint on a different source IP, the server may drop them or the return path gets broken. Two fixes: 1) increase the metric on the dock Ethernet so WireGuard's virtual adapter is preferred for the VPC routes, or 2) add a more specific persistent route for the VPC via the WireGuard interface.
mark: Example (PowerShell Admin):
```powershell
# show interfaces
Get-NetIPInterface | ft ifIndex,InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,InterfaceMetric
# set WireGuard adapter lower metric (more preferred) - use your adapter alias
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "WireGuard" -InterfaceMetric 5
# optional: bump dock ethernet metric higher
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Dock Ethernet" -InterfaceMetric 50
# confirm
Get-NetIPInterface | ft ifIndex,InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,InterfaceMetric
# persistent route alternative (example for 10.240.0.0/16) - replace <WireGuardGateway> and <ifIndex>
route -p ADD 10.240.0.0 MASK 255.255.0.0 <WireGuardGateway> IF <ifIndex>
```
ella: I changed the metrics to prefer WireGuard and ran `wsl --shutdown` and restarted WSL. Now `ping git.redwood.internal` from WSL resolves and `git clone` works. Woohoo. :tada:
it-support: Nice! Two gotchas to watch: 1) corporate MDM (Intune) can reset interface metrics or prevent persistent route changes; if the metric flips back after reboot, open a ticket with Device Management. 2) If you undock/roam, you might want a small script that resets metrics depending on whether docked or not.
ella: Yeah, after a reboot the metric reset. Is there a safe way to make the change reapply on login?
mark: We usually add a tiny scheduled task that runs at user login (runs as SYSTEM or local admin) to enforce the metric or re-add the persistent route. Example powershell scheduled task snippet (run once to create):
```powershell\$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'Powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias ""WireGuard"" -InterfaceMetric 5"'
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "RedwoodVPNMetricFix" -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn) -Action $action -RunLevel Highest -User "NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM"
```
mark: If you're not Admin to create the task, Device Management can push it centrally.
ella: Device Management created a policy entry to keep it consistent. One last thing: Docker Desktop in WSL still couldn't pull the registry until I toggled "Use the WSL 2 based engine" integration for my distro and restarted Docker.
it-support: Right — Docker's networking can be on a separate stack. Good checklist: 1) prefer WireGuard via interface metric or persistent route, 2) wsl --shutdown after route changes, 3) ensure Docker Desktop WSL integration enabled for your distro, 4) if MDM blocks changes, ask Device Management to push a scheduled task or route.
devops-bot: Docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/multi-nic-windows-vpn (add note: Surface dock metrics + WSL2) :white_check_mark:
ella: Thanks all, will add my step-by-step (including the scheduled task snippet provided by mark) to #new-hires so other docked folks don't get stuck. Really appreciate the quick help!
mark: Welcome aboard Ella! :wave: If anyone wants, I can add a small UI checklist in the device enrollment docs that runs these checks automatically.
ella: That would be awesome.
